angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 438,291 km at 189.01 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.2906 +/- 0.0186 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 189.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.63 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Gan et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract): 438,291 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.61 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Gan et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3794 +/- 79 K from Gan et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gan et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4201.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.625, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4201 (pscomppars): spectral type M1.0+/-0.5, from Gan et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4201 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.52 dex, from Gan et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4201 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.11919, from Gan et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4201 (pscomppars): age 1.4 Gyr, from Gan et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4201 (pscomppars): rotation period 17.3 d, from Gan et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..165G/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4201 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.65 km/s, from Gan et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...969L..24G/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.63 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.896. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
